description.value: The study investigated structural gray matter volume and cerebral blood flow abnormalities in phenocopy frontotemporal dementia, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls using regional quantitative MRI.

spans.text: We aimed to identify abnormalities in gray matter (GM) volume and perfusion in phFTD and to assess whether phFTD belongs to the FTD spectrum.

value: There were significant differences in nGM volume between groups mostly in frontal and temporal regions. PhFTD patients had lower supratentorial nGM volume than controls, most pronounced in the right posterior temporal lobe, right superior temporal gyrus and bilateral fusiform gyrus. BvFTD showed extensive bilateral frontotemporal nGM volume loss compared to controls.
This spectrum of findings, with mean nGM volumes being highest in controls, lowest in bvFTD and in-between in phFTD, was particularly apparent in the frontal and temporal lobes.

value: Compared to phFTD, bvFTD showed lower nGM volume in the right hippocampal formation and the right amygdala. Other nGM volumes were not significantly different between bvFTD and phFTD.
These findings suggest that there is a continuum in nGM volumes ranging from normal in controls to clearly abnormal in bvFTD, with phFTD in-between.

value: CBF in the bilateral subcallosal area was higher in phFTD than in both bvFTD and controls. BvFTD showed lower CBF than phFTD in the left superior and inferior frontal gyrus, the left orbitofrontal gyrus, and the bilateral straight gyrus; bvFTD also showed lower CBF than controls in the left inferior frontal and straight gyrus and the left orbitofrontal gyrus.
The higher perfusion in phFTD may reflect a compensatory process of increased activity to compensate for incipient pathology in regions affected in bvFTD.
